headline: Every tub of yoghurt checked, not a sample.
label: #FFFFFF
heroLede: Bega Group is investing about $110 million in new yoghurt, cream cheese and milk drink capacity, and its Morwell yoghurt plant is going through what the CEO called a significant transformation. New lines are the easiest place to build checks in from day one. This is what a camera check could look like on a yoghurt tub line. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every tub has its lid on, seated flat, with the foil seal intact underneath where it can be seen. A lifted lid on a yoghurt tub means leaks in the case and a complaint from the store.
labelLede: Natural and vanilla tubs can look much the same at line speed, and the wrong label can mean a missed allergen or a wrong claim. The camera checks every tub carries the right label for the run, straight and intact.
codeLede: Chilled yoghurt has a short use-by window, so the date has to be right and readable on every tub. The system reads the printed date and batch code and compares them with the product and date set at changeover.
objectLede: Glove pieces, lid offcuts and loose machine parts can end up close to the line. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a case.
